newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER - MALDINI TO BE NEXT ITALY COACH - PAPERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER - MALDINI TO BE NEXT ITALY COACH - PAPERS.

text.p: Former Italy captain Cesare Maldini will be the next national coach, Italian newspapers reported on Thursday.
The three main daily sports papers all agreed that under-21 coach Maldini would fill the vacancy left by Arrigo Sacchi once the new federation (FIGC) chairman is elected on December 14.

The federation commissioner Rafaele Pagnozzi, running the FIGC in the absence of an elected chairman, and Luciano Nizzola, the man sure to take over, met on Wednesday night and the newspapers said they had agreed on Maldini.
"Maldini the new coach, (Marco) Tardelli returns as his deputy," said the Corriere dello Sport.
"It's decided. Maldini gets the national team," added the Gazzetta dello Sport. "The announcement will be made after Nizzola is elected but the deal has been agreed."

Nizzola, saying he did not want to act as if he were chairman until actually elected, declined to give details on Wednesday but confirmed that an announcement would be made shortly after December 14 with no surprise names.

Maldini, father of Italy captain Paolo Maldini, has coached the under-21 team to three European titles and, despite failure at the Atlanta Olympics, has gained much prestige with impressive recent showings by his team.
Apart from being a popular choice, although less so than the 1982 World Cup-winning goalkeeper Dino Zoff, Maldini is also likely to be the cheapest option available.
If he is selected, it would mark a return to the pre-Sacchi days when a succession of Italy coaches were chosen "in-house" rather than recruited from the league clubs.

The vacancy arose after Sacchi, who had been widely expected to be dismissed by Nizzola despite a contract to coach Italy until the 1998 World Cup finals in France, suddenly resigned on Sunday night to return to his old club AC Milan.
Milan were bundled out of the European Cup by Norway's Rosenborg 2-1 on Wednesday night in their first match under Sacchi, who coached them to two European Cups in 1989 and 1990.
